Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., May 27, 1920/ Mr. Ben Benson, Chignik, Alaska. Dear Sir: Replying to your letter of May 2, 1920, in regard to your daughter, I have to inform you that this school closed permanently on May 14th. Elsie was sent to Mrs. Lunden at Astoria, Oregon. If you wish to place her in another Indian school, you should make application for her enrollment in Chemawa Indian School, Chemawa, Oregon. Mr. Harwood Hall is the Superintendent of Chemawa School. Yours respectfully, Clerk in Charge. Chignik, Alaska, May 2, 1920 Superintendent Cushman School, Tacoma, Wash., Dear sir: On her way to Chignik, Alaska, Mrs. Osmond called at the school to see my daughter and was informed that the school would close in June on account of not sufficient funds. If this is correct, I would like to have you send my daughter to Mrs. Lundine, 385 Twenty seventh street, Astoria, Oregon. In any event, I would like to have her sent there for her vacation. When I sent her to the Cushman School I signed for three years, which time will expire next October. If possible, I would like my daughter to remain for three years longer under the same conditions as before. I can not very well afford to pay for this as I am now paying for two other children here in Alaska. In the event of the school remaining open, I would appreciate it very much if you would notify me. Thanking you in advance, I am, Very truly yours, Ben Benson File - Elsie Benson Mrs. Josephine Lunden #385 = 27th St - Astoria Oregon Astoria, Oregon, 385 - 24th St., Aug. 25 - 1919. Cushman School Dear Mr. Hammond: I must now let you know that Elsie Benson is returning to school next Thursday. She will leave here on the morning train going through Portland. Will you please be so kind as to meet her on the station when the train arrives, as she will be coming back alone. Elvie has enjoyed her summer and I hope she will continue with her studies as before. Please be so kind and meet her. Sincerely yours, Olga Sunderland TO OFFICER SENDING TELEGRAM. 1. Cushman School, Mr. Hammond: Dear Sir: Received your telegram this morning concerning Elsie Benson, in which you stated that you could not send her down alone. It is kind of hard for me at this parent and so she would only have a few weeks to stay. It would not really pay to come as the fare is so high. I still ask you, if it would be alright, if you would get the ticket straight through to Astoria, and ask the conductor on the train to look a little after. I have seen younger ones than she is traveling alone. If this cannot be done and she is anxious to come, please wire me, I will pay charges and come for her as soon as possible. Therfing that you would try your best, and I would be very thankful to you. Very sincerely yours, Mrs. Elga Anderson, 38 S - 29th St, Astoria, Oregon. Astoria, Oregon, July 12-1918. Dear Miss Benson, I am again sending you a few lines, and wish to ask you, for the reason that you have not answered my letters. If I do not hear from you in a few days, I am going to write to the Superintendent of the school so as to find out more about you. We have been waiting much on your account. Now if that money was not enough to come over here, why have you not written and asked for some more. Now answer as soon as you receive this, I am wishing for you to come and see me. Ethel is anxiously waiting for you. Answer soon, your friend: Mrs. Olga Andersen, 385 - 27th St, Astoria, Oregon VACATION REQUEST FOR PUPIL. We, the undersigned, respectfully request that leave of absence be granted Elsie Brown from June 1st to October 1st to enable her to visit her home. We hereby agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. We further agree that said pupil shall be returned to the Cushman Trade school on or before the last day of the leave of absence. We further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient money to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the pupils, or any one of them, fail to return to school at such time as may be agreed upon by the parents or guardian and the superintendent of the school in which the pupils are enrolled, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the pupil or pupils so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government; provided, however, that in all cases where it can be shown that there were justifiable reasons for the failure of the return of the pupil the forfeiture of the funds shall not take place. If the pupil neglecting to return is from a reservation, the superintendent of the reservation shall certify to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. If a pupil's home is not on a reservation, then the certificate of some reputable, disinterested citizen of the community may be requested as to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. Father. Mother. Mr. & Mrs. Henry Moy Guardian. Date: May 24th 1918 NOTE TO DISBURSING OFFICERS.—All receipts under this agreement must be accounted for officially as Individual Indian Money. However, any forfeitures must be transferred to Miscellaneous Receipts, Class I, and deposited in the Treasury to the credit of the United States. Hoonah, Alaska May 24, 1918 Cushman Trade School Tacoma, Wash. Dear Sir: Your letter of May 16th regarding my sister-in-law Elsie Brown has been received. As she is to stay with us this summer, we are taking the liberty of signing for her vacation. Her father has left her with her Aunt quite while and the usual method of the older folks are to let the child work all summer and take most of the earnings. We therefore hope by having her stay with us, when she leaves for school this fall to have it all to her credit. I am enclosing $13. to make up for what she has drawn of the $33.00 necessary as a deposit. We will see that she returns this fall as we expect to go South. I think she will have to go to Juneau and then take the weekly mail boat from here to Hoonah. The mail boat fare is $5.00. Thanking you for your kindness in this matter. Mr. Hawksworth, Supt. of Alaska Native Schools are a personal friend of Mine. H. Pkg. G. Henry Moy Hoonah, Alaska THE CUSHMAN TRADES SCHOOL TACOMA, WASHINGTON. July 29th, 1918. Mrs. Olga Anderson. 305-27th Street. Astoria, Ore. Dear Mr. Anderson, As you will see by the enclosed letter and envelope, I answered promptly your enquiry about Elsie Fenson and returned your ten dollars to you. A Mr. or Mrs. Anderson opened the letter and returned it and its contents to me. Elsie's father has written her since that she could visit you and she may do so on condition of being promptly returned to school, September 5th, 1918. I am sorry she has missed so much of her visit but as I am responsible for the children entrusted to me, I must insist on the parent's written consent to a pupil visiting friends or relatives. Very sincerely yours, Superintendent. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington June 12, 1918. Mrs. A. Anderson Astoria, Oregon. Dear Madam, Enclosed herewith you will find the ten dollars which you sent to Elsie Benson to pay her fare to Astoria. Elsie was entered in this school by her father and I have not the authority to permit her to spend her vacation with you unless I have her father's consent. If her father is willing that Elsie should spend her vacation with you and will write me to that effect, I have no objections to Elsie's visiting you. Very respectfully, Superintendent 385 - 27th St, Astoria Oregon, June 18-19 Cushman School Dear Sir: Some time ago I wrote to you for information about Elsie Benson, but have received no answer. Now as the term is soon coming to an end I would be very glad to know if she is going to get her vacation, for I think she should as she was disappointed last year. I have noticed from her letters that she would be very glad to come here, and you surely could trust her to come, can't she would be back back for the time that school opens again. I am here enclosing Ten dollars for Elsie's fare, if not enough please let me know, in time so that I may send more. In case she does not get off please send the money back, as she does not need it over there. I am also enclosing a postage stamp, so will expect an early answer. Yours truly, Alga Lunden, 385 - 27th St, Astoria, Oregon P.S. Please hand this envelope to Elsie Benson, and please answer right away, if she comes or not. Same. Received $10.00 for expenses to Astoria Elsie Benson Astoria Oregon, June 10-1918. Dear Chic: I received your letter a few days ago and was very glad to hear that you are well and will get your summer vacation. We are hearing from you so you can get down here. Now Chic, you ask the teacher or some grown-up person to get your ticket for you from there, right straight to Astoria, so you will not have any worry about that, and as soon as you get this drop me a few lines and let us know when you come, that we may be down to meet you. I must also tell you that I am married now, with Andersen, do you remember him yet? So be a good girl until I see you. Lovingly your friend, Mrs. A. Remarks: ..................................................................................................................................................................................... 385 - 27th St, Astoria, Oregon, May 19, 1919 Superintendent of School, Dear Sir: I must now trouble you about Elsie Benson, and find out if she is to get her summer vacation this year. Her father has written to me and said that he would arrange everything so that she will get off as soon as the time ends. Mrs. Armond told me that she was going to stop there on her way to Alaska, and leave some money there for Elsie's trip, and then the money or ten dollars from last year has Elsie been spending it? Please let me know and if she gets off we will send the money if there is none. Then would you be so kind and get the ticket for her, straight through and give her a note which she could show the conductor on the train, we will be here to meet her, when she arrives. Please let me know. I remain truly yours truly, Ada Lunden CASE RECORD.
